title: PS-Characters And Endo-Classes
body_html:
PS-Characters And Endo-Classes

Let $(E,\beta)$ be a simple based extension of $F$. A ps-character supported on $\beta$ is a transfer-compatible rule assigning to every triple

$$ (V,\varphi,x) $$

a simple character in $\mathcal C(x,\varphi(\beta))$, where:

  • $V$ is a finite-dimensional $F$-vector space;
  • $\varphi:E\hookrightarrow\operatorname{End}_F(V)$ is an embedding, so $V$ is viewed as an $E$-vector space;
  • $x$ is a point in the building of $\operatorname{GL}_{\varphi(E)}(V)$.

A simple character in the image of a ps-character is called a realization.

Two ps-characters are equivalent if there exist realizations on a common $F$-vector space $V$ which intertwine in $\operatorname{GL}_F(V)$. The draft states that this is equivalent to asking that any realizations on a common vector space intertwine.

An endo-class is an equivalence class of ps-characters. The set of endo-classes over $F$ is denoted

$$ \mathscr E(F). $$

The unique endo-class supported on $0$ is the trivial endo-class $\mathfrak c_0$. The non-trivial endo-classes form

$$ \mathscr E^+(F):=\mathscr E(F)\setminus\{\mathfrak c_0\}. $$
